_comment: Short plain-language descriptions shown in the side panel. Keys are item names as displayed; 'Parent › Item' keys override a plain name where the same name means different things in different places. Items without an entry get a generic line.

spending.Department of Health and Human Services: Runs Medicare and Medicaid (through CMS) plus the public health agencies: NIH, CDC, FDA, the Indian Health Service, and family and child programs.
spending.Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Servic: Pays for health care for people 65 and older and some people with disabilities (Medicare), and the federal share of state Medicaid and CHIP programs.
spending.Federal Supplementary Medical Insurance: Medicare Parts B and D: doctor visits, outpatient care and prescription drugs. Funded mainly by general tax revenue plus enrollee premiums.
Medicare Part B: payments for doctor visits, outpatient hospital care, lab tests and medical equipment.
spending.Medicare Prescription Drugs: Medicare Part D: subsidies for prescription drug plans covering Medicare enrollees.
spending.Federal Hospital Insurance Trust Fund: Medicare Part A: inpatient hospital stays, skilled nursing, hospice and some home health care. Funded mainly by the 2.9% Medicare payroll tax.
spending.Federal Hospital Insurance Trust Fund ›: Medicare Part A payments to hospitals, skilled nursing facilities and hospices.
spending.Administrative Expenses: The cost of running the program itself: staff, claims processing, systems and offices.
spending.Grants to States for Medicaid: The federal share of Medicaid, the joint federal-state health program for low-income people. The federal government pays roughly 50% to 77% of each state's costs, more for poorer states.
spending.Children's Health Insurance Fund: Federal funding for CHIP, which covers children in families that earn too much for Medicaid but cannot afford private coverage.
spending.Administration for Children and Families: Grants to states for child care, foster care, child support enforcement, cash assistance (TANF), Head Start and refugee resettlement.
spending.Temporary Assistance for Needy Families: TANF block grants that states use for cash assistance, work programs and other support for low-income families with children.
spending.Children and Families Services Programs: Mostly Head Start, the early-childhood education program, plus child abuse prevention and community services grants.
spending.Payments to States for Foster Care and A: Federal share of state foster care, adoption assistance and kinship guardianship payments.
spending.Payments to States for the Child Care an: Grants that help low-income working families pay for child care.
spending.Payments to States for Child Support Enf: Federal share of state programs that locate parents and collect child support.
spending.Low Income Home Energy Assistance: LIHEAP: help with heating and cooling bills for low-income households.
spending.Refugee and Entrant Assistance: Resettlement support for refugees, and care for unaccompanied migrant children.
spending.National Institutes of Health: The main federal funder of biomedical research, mostly grants to universities and hospitals plus its own labs in Bethesda.
spending.Health Resources and Services Administra: Funds community health centers, rural health, HIV/AIDS care (Ryan White), maternal and child health and the organ transplant system.
spending.Indian Health Service: Provides health care to members of federally recognized tribes, directly and through tribal health programs.
spending.Centers for Disease Control and Preventi: Disease tracking and prevention, vaccine purchases for low-income children, and grants to state and local health departments.
spending.Substance Abuse and Mental Health Servic: Grants for addiction treatment, opioid response and mental health services, including the 988 crisis line.
spending.Social Security Administration: Pays Social Security retirement, survivors and disability benefits, and Supplemental Security Income.
spending.Federal Old-Age and Survivors Insurance: Social Security retirement and survivors benefits, paid to more than 60 million retirees, spouses and children of deceased workers. Funded by the 12.4% payroll tax.
spending.Federal Disability Insurance Trust Fund: Social Security Disability Insurance, paid to workers who can no longer work because of a disability, and their dependents.
spending.Federal Old-Age and Survivors Insurance: Monthly Social Security checks to retirees, their spouses and survivors.
spending.Federal Disability Insurance Trust Fund: Monthly disability benefits to disabled workers and their dependents.
spending.Supplemental Security Income Program: Monthly cash payments to low-income people who are aged, blind or disabled, funded from general revenue rather than payroll taxes.
spending.Department of the Treasury: Mostly interest on the national debt, plus the IRS, refundable tax credits paid out as refunds, and the government's payment and debt-management operations.
spending.Interest on the Public Debt: Interest the Treasury pays on the money it has borrowed. Interest paid to federal trust funds is excluded here as an internal transfer.
spending.Interest on Treasury Debt Securities (Gr: Interest on Treasury bills, notes, bonds and other securities.
spending.Interest paid to the public (marketable: Interest on debt held by investors, banks, foreign governments and the Federal Reserve. This is the real cost of borrowing to cover deficits.
spending.Internal Revenue Service: Tax collection and enforcement, plus the refundable parts of tax credits, which the budget counts as spending.
spending.Refundable Premium Tax Credits and Cost: Affordable Care Act subsidies that lower premiums and out-of-pocket costs for people buying insurance on the health exchanges.
spending.Payment Where Earned Income Credit Excee: The refundable part of the Earned Income Tax Credit: money paid to low- and moderate-income workers beyond what they owed in tax.
spending.Payment Where Child Tax Credit Exceeds L: The refundable part of the Child Tax Credit, paid to families whose credit exceeds the tax they owe.
spending.Payment Where American Opportunity Tax C: The refundable part of the college tuition tax credit.
spending.Refunding Internal Revenue Collections,: Interest the IRS pays taxpayers on refunds that were issued late.
spending.Enforcement: IRS audits, collections and criminal investigations.
spending.Operations Support: IRS technology, facilities and other support functions.
spending.Taxpayer Services: IRS help lines, taxpayer assistance centers and return processing.
spending.Bureau of the Fiscal Service: The government's payment, collection and debt-accounting operations.
spending.Interest Paid to Credit Financing Accoun: Interest Treasury pays to the accounts that hold federal loan programs' cash.
spending.Claims, Judgements, and Relief Acts: The Judgment Fund, which pays court judgments and legal settlements against the federal government.
spending.Departmental Offices: Department-level offices and programs not assigned to a specific bureau.
spending.Department of Defense (Military): The armed forces: pay, operations, weapons purchases, research and construction. Regrouped here by service. Military retirement is listed separately under Defense Civil Programs.
spending.Navy & Marine Corps: The Department of the Navy, which includes the Marine Corps.
spending.Air Force & Space Force: The Department of the Air Force, which includes the Space Force.
spending.Army: The Department of the Army, including the Army National Guard and Army Reserve.
spending.Defense-wide Agencies: Agencies serving all services: the Defense Health Program, Missile Defense Agency, special operations, intelligence, DARPA and others.
spending.Operation and Maintenance: Day-to-day costs: training, fuel, maintenance, depots, base operations, civilian staff and military health care.
spending.Procurement: Buying weapons and equipment: aircraft, ships, vehicles, missiles, ammunition and communications gear.
spending.Military Personnel: Pay, allowances, housing and benefits for active-duty and reserve troops, plus contributions to their retirement and health funds.
spending.Research, Development, Test, and Evaluat: Developing and testing new systems, from basic science to prototypes and flight tests.
spending.Military Construction: Building and renovating facilities on military bases, in the U.S. and overseas.
spending.Family Housing: Building, leasing and maintaining housing for military families.
spending.Revolving and Management Funds: Working capital funds and other business-like DoD funds.
spending.Working Capital Fund: Revolving funds that run depots, supply chains and transportation services and charge units for them.
spending.Trust Funds: Small accounts funded by gifts and specific receipts.
spending.Defense Civil Programs (Military Retirem: Military retiree pensions and health care for Medicare-eligible military retirees (TRICARE for Life).
spending.Military Retirement: Pensions for retired military members and survivor annuities.
spending.Military Retirement Fund: The fund that pays monthly retired pay to former service members.
spending.Retiree Health Care: Health coverage for military retirees who are also on Medicare.
spending.Department of Defense Medicare-Eligible: TRICARE for Life: pays costs Medicare does not cover for military retirees 65 and older.
spending.Department of Veterans Affairs: Disability compensation and pensions for veterans, the VA health system, the GI Bill and veterans' home loans.
spending.Benefits Programs: Cash benefits paid to veterans and their families.
spending.Compensation and Pensions: Monthly disability compensation for service-connected conditions, and needs-based pensions for low-income wartime veterans.
spending.Readjustment Benefits: Mostly the GI Bill: tuition, housing and training benefits for veterans.
spending.Veterans Health Administration: The VA hospital and clinic system, the largest integrated health system in the country.
spending.Medical Services: Direct patient care at VA hospitals and clinics, plus care VA purchases from community providers.
spending.Medical Support and Compliance: Management and administration for the VA health system.
spending.Medical Facilities: Operating and maintaining VA hospitals and clinics.
spending.Information Technology Systems: Technology systems, including the VA electronic health record.
spending.Department of Agriculture: Nutrition programs (SNAP, school meals, WIC), farm support and crop insurance, the Forest Service and rural development.
spending.Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Progra: SNAP (formerly food stamps): monthly benefits on an EBT card for low-income households to buy groceries.
spending.Child Nutrition Programs: Free and reduced-price school lunch and breakfast, summer meals and child-care meals.
spending.Special Supplemental Nutrition Program f: Food benefits, nutrition counseling and formula for low-income pregnant women, new mothers and young children.
spending.Federal Crop Insurance Corporation Fund: Subsidizes insurance premiums and covers losses on crop insurance sold to farmers through private insurers.
spending.Forest Service: Manages 193 million acres of national forests and grasslands and fights wildfires.
spending.Wildland Fire Management: Wildfire suppression, preparedness and fuel reduction.
spending.Farm Service Agency: Farm loans, commodity price and income support, and disaster aid for farmers.
spending.Commodity Credit Corporation: Pays farm commodity support programs such as price-loss and revenue coverage, and funds conservation and trade-aid programs.
spending.Natural Resources Conservation Service: Pays farmers to adopt conservation practices on working land.
spending.Department of Education: Student aid for college (Pell grants and federal student loans) and grants to schools for low-income students and special education.
spending.Office of Federal Student Aid: Pell grants, federal student loans and work-study.
spending.Federal Direct Student Loans: The budget cost of federal student loans: the estimated subsidy on new loans and revisions to past loans' estimated costs. Loan amounts lent and repaid are not counted here.
spending.Student Financial Assistance: Mostly Pell grants for low-income college students, plus work-study and other grants.
spending.Federal Family Education Loans: Costs of the older guaranteed student loan program, which stopped making new loans in 2010.
spending.Office of Elementary and Secondary Educa: Grants to school districts, mostly for schools with many low-income students.
spending.Accelerating Achievement and Ensuring Eq: Mainly Title I grants to school districts serving high numbers of low-income students.
spending.Education Improvement Programs: Other K-12 grant programs run by the Office of Elementary and Secondary Education.
spending.Office of Special Education and Rehabili: Special education grants to states and vocational rehabilitation for people with disabilities.
spending.Special Education: IDEA grants that help states and schools pay for educating students with disabilities.
spending.Rehabilitation Services and Disability R: Vocational rehabilitation services that help people with disabilities find work.
spending.Office of Postsecondary Education: Grants to colleges, including minority-serving institutions and TRIO programs.
spending.Office of Personnel Management: Pays retirement and health benefits for retired federal civilian employees.
spending.Civil Service Retirement and Disability: Pension payments to retired federal civilian employees and their survivors.
spending.Government Payment for Annuitants, Emplo: The government's share of health insurance premiums for retired federal employees.
spending.Postal Service Retiree Health Benefits F: Health benefits for retired Postal Service employees.
spending.Department of Homeland Security: Border and immigration enforcement, the Coast Guard, airport screening, FEMA disaster relief and the Secret Service.
spending.Federal Emergency Management Agency: Disaster response and recovery aid, and the National Flood Insurance Program.
spending.Disaster Relief: Aid to states, communities and individuals after declared disasters such as hurricanes, floods and wildfires.
spending.U.S. Customs and Border Protection: Border Patrol, ports-of-entry inspections and customs enforcement.
spending.Immigration and Customs Enforcement: Immigration enforcement, detention and removals, and Homeland Security Investigations.
spending.United States Coast Guard: Maritime safety, search and rescue, drug and migrant interdiction, and port security.
spending.Citizenship and Immigration Services: Processes visas, green cards, naturalization and asylum applications, funded mostly by application fees.
spending.Department of Transportation: Grants for highways, transit and airports, plus the air traffic control system and rail programs.
spending.Highway Trust Fund: Fund financed mostly by federal fuel taxes that pays for highway and transit grants.
spending.Federal-Aid Highways: Formula grants that reimburse states for building and repairing highways and bridges.
spending.Federal Aviation Administration: Air traffic control, aviation safety and airport grants.
spending.Airport and Airway Trust Fund: Fund financed by airline ticket and fuel taxes that pays for the FAA and airport grants.
spending.Trust Fund Share of FAA Operations: The portion of air traffic control operations paid from aviation taxes.
spending.Federal Transit Administration: Grants to local transit agencies for buses, rail and capital projects.
spending.Transit Formula Grants: Formula grants that help transit agencies buy vehicles and maintain systems.
spending.Federal Railroad Administration: Grants to Amtrak and to passenger and freight rail projects, plus rail safety.
spending.Department of Housing and Urban Developm: Rental assistance for low-income households, public housing, community development grants and FHA mortgage insurance.
spending.Tenant Based Rental Assistance: Housing Choice Vouchers (Section 8): help for about 2.3 million low-income households to rent in the private market.
spending.Public Housing Operating Fund: Operating subsidies for public housing authorities.
spending.Housing Programs: Rental assistance tied to specific buildings, housing for the elderly and disabled, and FHA mortgage insurance.
spending.HUD Project-Based Rental Assistance: Section 8 contracts with private landlords that keep specific apartments affordable.
spending.Credit Accounts: FHA mortgage insurance programs. Large negative entries are premiums and reestimates flowing back to the government.
spending.Community Planning and Development: Flexible grants to cities and states, homelessness programs and disaster housing recovery.
spending.Community Development Fund: Community Development Block Grants and disaster recovery grants.
spending.International Assistance Programs: Foreign aid, military aid to allies and the foreign military sales program.
spending.Military Sales Program: Weapons the U.S. buys on behalf of foreign governments, which pay in advance. Their payments offset nearly all of it.
spending.Foreign Military Sales Trust Fund: Payments to U.S. defense contractors for weapons sold to foreign governments.
spending.International Security Assistance: Military aid and economic support to allies and partners.
spending.Foreign Military Financing Program: Grants and loans that let allies buy U.S. weapons and training.
spending.Agency for International Development: Payments from foreign aid accounts historically run by USAID, including humanitarian and development assistance.
spending.International Disaster Assistance: Emergency humanitarian aid overseas: food, shelter and health care after disasters and conflicts.
spending.Department of Labor: Mostly unemployment insurance, plus job training and workers' compensation for federal employees.
spending.Employment and Training Administration: Unemployment insurance and job training programs.
spending.Unemployment Trust Fund: Pays state unemployment benefits from payroll taxes that employers pay to states.
spending.Federal-State Unemployment Insurance: Unemployment benefits run by states under federal rules.
spending.State Unemployment Benefits: Weekly unemployment checks to laid-off workers.
spending.State Administrative Expenses: Federal grants that pay for states to run their unemployment systems.
spending.Office of Workers' Compensation Programs: Workers' compensation for federal employees, coal miners with black lung disease and nuclear-weapons workers.
spending.Department of Energy: Mostly nuclear weapons and environmental cleanup of former weapons sites, plus science research and energy programs.
spending.National Nuclear Security Administration: Maintains the nuclear weapons stockpile, builds naval reactors and runs nonproliferation programs.
spending.Weapons Activities: Maintaining, modernizing and testing (without explosions) the nuclear weapons stockpile at labs such as Los Alamos and Sandia.
spending.Naval Reactors: Designs and maintains the nuclear reactors for Navy submarines and aircraft carriers.
spending.Energy Programs: Science research, energy technology and energy loan programs.
spending.Science: The DOE Office of Science: national labs, particle physics, fusion and supercomputing.
spending.Environmental and Other Defense Activiti: Cleanup of former nuclear weapons production sites.
spending.Defense Environmental Cleanup: Cleaning up radioactive and hazardous waste at sites like Hanford and Savannah River.
spending.Department of Justice: Federal law enforcement, prosecutors, the prison system and grants to state and local police.
spending.Legal Activities and U.S. Marshals: U.S. Attorneys, litigating divisions and the U.S. Marshals.
spending.General Legal Activities: DOJ's litigating divisions, such as the civil, criminal, antitrust and civil rights divisions.
spending.Federal Bureau of Investigation: Federal criminal investigations, counterterrorism and counterintelligence.
spending.Federal Prison System: The Bureau of Prisons, which runs federal prisons and residential reentry centers.
spending.Office of Justice Programs: Grants to state and local law enforcement, victim services and crime research.
spending.Independent Agencies: Smaller agencies outside the cabinet departments. Their totals include large offsetting receipts, such as FDIC insurance premiums.
spending.Railroad Retirement Board: Retirement and disability benefits for railroad workers, who are covered by this program instead of Social Security.
spending.Railroad Social Security Equivalent Bene: The portion of railroad retirement benefits that matches what Social Security would pay.
spending.Rail Industry Pension Fund: The portion of railroad retirement that works like a private pension on top of the Social Security-equivalent benefit.
spending.Federal Communications Commission: Telecommunications regulation and the Universal Service Fund.
spending.Universal Service Fund: Subsidies for phone and internet service in rural areas, schools, libraries and low-income households, funded by fees on phone companies.
spending.Department of State: Embassies and diplomacy, global health programs and contributions to international organizations.
spending.Administration of Foreign Affairs: Running the diplomatic service: embassies, consulates and passport services.
spending.Diplomatic and Consular Programs: Embassy staff and operations, diplomatic security and passport and visa services.
spending.Global Health and Child Survival: Global health programs, including PEPFAR for HIV/AIDS, malaria and maternal and child health.
spending.Department of the Interior: National parks, public lands, Bureau of Indian Affairs, water projects and payments to states from mineral leasing.
spending.Mineral Leasing and Associated Payments: States' share of royalties from oil, gas and coal leases on federal land.
spending.Department-Wide Programs: Wildland fire management on Interior lands and payments to counties that contain untaxable federal land.
spending.Fish and Wildlife and Parks: The National Park Service and the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service.
spending.National Park Service: Runs the 430+ national parks, monuments and historic sites.
spending.Water and Science: The Bureau of Reclamation (western dams and water projects) and the U.S. Geological Survey.
spending.National Aeronautics and Space Administr: Human spaceflight, science missions, aeronautics research and the space station.
spending.Exploration: The Artemis program to return astronauts to the Moon: the SLS rocket, Orion capsule and ground systems.
spending.Environmental Protection Agency: Environmental regulation and enforcement, plus grants for water infrastructure and Superfund cleanups.
spending.State and Tribal Assistance Grants: Mostly the clean water and drinking water revolving funds that finance local water infrastructure.
spending.Department of Commerce: Weather forecasting (NOAA), the Census Bureau, standards research (NIST) and trade and economic development programs.
spending.National Oceanic and Atmospheric Adminis: The National Weather Service, weather satellites, fisheries and ocean research.
spending.National Institute of Standards and Tech: Measurement science and standards, including CHIPS Act semiconductor manufacturing incentives.
spending.Small Business Administration: Loans, loan guarantees and disaster loans for small businesses and homeowners.
spending.Disaster Loans Program: Low-interest loans to businesses and homeowners recovering from declared disasters.
spending.Corps of Engineers: Army Corps of Engineers civil works: navigation channels, flood control, dams and ecosystem restoration.
spending.National Science Foundation: Grants for basic research and science education across non-medical fields.
spending.Research and Related Activities: NSF research grants to universities in fields from physics to computer science.
spending.Judicial Branch: The federal courts, public defenders and probation offices.
spending.Courts of Appeals, District Courts, and: Federal trial and appeals courts, plus defender services and probation.
spending.Legislative Branch: Congress and its support agencies: the Library of Congress, GAO, CBO and the Capitol Police.
spending.Executive Office of the President: White House offices and staff. Its net total is negative because of fee and receipt offsets.
spending.General Services Administration: Manages federal buildings and purchasing. Agency rent payments to GSA largely offset its costs.
spending.Proprietary Receipts from the Public: Money collected from the public in business-like transactions (fees, sales, premiums, loan repayments) that is recorded as negative spending.
spending.Air Force & Space Force › Procurement: Buying aircraft, missiles, munitions, satellites and equipment for the Air Force and Space Force. Over a third goes to classified programs.
spending.Air Force & Space Force › Research, Deve: Developing new systems for the Air Force and Space Force, including the B-21 bomber, F-47 fighter, Sentinel ICBM and missile-warning satellites. About a third of the funding is classified.
spending.Aircraft Procurement, Air Force: Buying new aircraft (F-35A, F-15EX, B-21, KC-46A tankers, C-130J) and modifying aircraft already in service.
spending.Missile Procurement, Air Force: Buying air-launched missiles such as AMRAAM and JASSM, plus missile modifications.
spending.Procurement of Ammunition, Air Force: Bombs, guidance kits like JDAM, fuzes, flares and small-arms ammunition.
spending.Other Procurement, Air Force: Vehicles, communications and electronics, base equipment, and most of the Air Force's classified procurement.
spending.Procurement, Space Force: Launch services and satellites for the Space Force, including national security launches and Space Development Agency constellations.
spending.RDT&E, Air Force: Air Force research and development, from basic science to engineering development and upgrades of fielded systems.
spending.RDT&E, Space Force: Space Force research and development, mainly missile-warning and tracking satellites, satellite communications and classified space programs.
spending.Combat Aircraft: Fighters, bombers and other combat aircraft.
spending.Modification of Inservice Aircraft: Upgrades to aircraft already in the fleet: new radars, engines, avionics and structural fixes for the F-22, F-16, B-52, C-17 and others.
spending.Aircraft Spares and Repair Parts: Initial spare parts for new and modified aircraft.
spending.Aircraft Support Equipment and Facilitie: Ground equipment, training simulators and industrial facilities that support aircraft.
spending.Other Base Maintenance and Support Equip: Base equipment and other support equipment.
spending.Electronics and Telecommunications Equip: Radios, networks, air traffic control, weather systems and base security electronics.
spending.Vehicular Equipment: Trucks, fire and crash-rescue vehicles, and other ground vehicles.
spending.Ammunition: Bombs, artillery rounds, cartridges, fuzes and other munitions.
spending.Not assigned to a budget activity: Outlays the account reported without assigning them to a budget activity, mostly from older appropriations.
spending.Basic Research: Scientific research without a specific weapon application, mostly grants to universities.
spending.Applied Research: Research aimed at specific military needs, such as materials, propulsion and sensors.
spending.Advanced Technology Development: Demonstrating technologies in realistic settings before they enter a program.
spending.Advanced Component Development and Proto: Building and testing prototypes of new systems before full development.
spending.System Development and Demonstration: Engineering and manufacturing development of systems headed for production.
spending.Management Support: Test ranges, test and evaluation infrastructure, and research management.
spending.Operational System Development: Upgrades to systems already fielded, plus most classified R&D.
spending.Software and Digital Technology Pilot Pr: Pilot programs that fund software as a single budget line instead of splitting it across R&D, procurement and operations.
spending.Classified Programs: Programs whose details are classified. The budget publishes only a total, so no further breakdown is available.
spending.B-21 Raider: Production of the B-21 stealth bomber, built by Northrop Grumman in Palmdale, California.
spending.F-35: F-35A Lightning II production for the Air Force. Lockheed Martin builds the airframe and Pratt & Whitney the F135 engine.
spending.F-35 C2D2: Continuous capability development and delivery for the F-35: software and hardware upgrades, including Block 4.
spending.F-15EX: New-build F-15EX Eagle II fighters from Boeing in St. Louis.
spending.F-47: Development of the F-47, the Next Generation Air Dominance sixth-generation fighter awarded to Boeing in 2025.
spending.KC-46A MDAP: KC-46A Pegasus aerial refueling tankers from Boeing.
spending.C-130J: C-130J Super Hercules transports from Lockheed Martin.
spending.Ground Based Strategic Deterrent EMD: Engineering and manufacturing development of the LGM-35A Sentinel ICBM, which replaces Minuteman III.
spending.Survivable Airborne Operations Center (S: Replacement for the E-4B 'doomsday' airborne command post.
spending.E-7: E-7 Wedgetail airborne early warning and control aircraft, replacing the E-3 AWACS.
spending.Collaborative Combat Aircraft: Uncrewed aircraft designed to fly alongside crewed fighters.
spending.Advanced Battle Management System (ABMS): Networks and software that connect sensors and shooters across the Air Force.
spending.B-52 Squadrons: B-52 upgrades, including the Commercial Engine Replacement Program and new radar.
spending.F-22A Squadrons: F-22 Raptor upgrades and sustainment development.
spending.F-22A: Modifications to F-22 Raptors in service.
spending.VC-25B: The two new Air Force One aircraft, based on the Boeing 747-8.
spending.Joint Air-Surface Standoff Missile: JASSM, a stealthy long-range air-launched cruise missile from Lockheed Martin.
spending.National Security Space Launch: Launch services for national security satellites, provided by SpaceX, United Launch Alliance and Blue Origin.
spending.Resilient Missile Warning Missile Tracki: A low-orbit constellation of satellites that detect and track missile launches, including hypersonic weapons.
Missile-warning satellites in medium Earth orbit.
spending.Space-Based Moving Target Indicator: Satellites to track moving targets on the ground from space.
spending.Evolved Strategic SATCOM (ESS): Next-generation protected satellite communications for nuclear command and control.
spending.Test and Evaluation Support: Operating Air Force test ranges and facilities, such as Edwards and Eglin.
spending.General Purpose Bombs: Unguided bomb bodies that guidance kits like JDAM turn into precision weapons.
spending.Joint Direct Attack Munition: JDAM guidance kits that turn unguided bombs into GPS-guided weapons.
spending.Navy & Marine Corps › Procurement: Ships, submarines, aircraft, missiles and equipment for the Navy and Marine Corps. Shipbuilding is the largest share.
spending.Navy & Marine Corps › Research, Developm: Navy and Marine Corps R&D, including the F/A-XX next-generation fighter, nuclear deterrent programs and hypersonic strike.
spending.Army › Procurement: Helicopters, air and missile defense interceptors, armored vehicles, ammunition and communications gear for the Army.
spending.Army › Research, Development, Test, and: Army R&D, including the Future Long Range Assault Aircraft, hypersonic weapons, air and missile defense and combat-vehicle upgrades.
spending.Shipbuilding and Conversion, Navy: Building new ships and submarines and refueling aircraft carriers. Ships take five or more years to build, so most of this year's spending pays for ships funded years ago.
spending.Aircraft Procurement, Navy: Navy and Marine Corps aircraft: F-35B and F-35C, CH-53K helicopters, E-2D Hawkeyes, KC-130J tankers, and upgrades to aircraft in service.
spending.Other Procurement, Navy: Ship equipment and modernization, communications, unmanned surface vessels, aviation and ordnance support equipment, and spares.
spending.Weapons Procurement, Navy: Trident II D5 missile upkeep, Standard Missiles, Tomahawks, LRASM, torpedoes and mines.
spending.Maritime Industrial Base Fund: New fund to expand shipyard and supplier capacity for submarine and surface-ship construction.
spending.Procurement, Marine Corps: Marine Corps vehicles, weapons, air defense, communications and engineering equipment.
spending.Procurement of Ammunition, Navy & Marine: Ammunition, loitering munitions, artillery rounds and countermeasures for the Navy and Marine Corps.
spending.National Sea-Based Deterrence Fund: Fund created to pay for Columbia-class ballistic missile submarines outside the regular shipbuilding account. It still pays out on earlier years' funding.
spending.RDT&E, Navy: Navy and Marine Corps research and development.
spending.Aircraft Procurement, Army: Army helicopters (UH-60M Black Hawk, CH-47 Chinook, AH-64 Apache), drones and aircraft survivability equipment.
spending.Missile Procurement, Army: Patriot PAC-3 MSE interceptors, GMLRS rockets, the Precision Strike Missile, short-range air defense and the Dark Eagle hypersonic missile.
spending.Weapons & Tracked Combat Vehicles, Army: Abrams tanks, Paladin howitzers, Armored Multi-Purpose Vehicles, Bradley and Stryker upgrades, and small arms such as the Next Generation Squad Weapon.
spending.Procurement of Ammunition, Army: Artillery, tank and small-arms ammunition, plus modernizing the Army's government-owned ammunition plants.
spending.Other Procurement, Army: Trucks and tactical vehicles, radios and networks, counter-drone systems, air defense command systems and other equipment.
spending.Fleet Ballistic Missile Ships: Columbia-class ballistic missile submarines, which will carry the sea-based leg of the nuclear deterrent.
spending.Other Warships: Attack submarines, destroyers, aircraft carriers and carrier refueling overhauls.
spending.Amphibious Ships: Ships that carry Marines and their equipment: LPDs, LHAs and the new Medium Landing Ship.
spending.Modification of Aircraft: Upgrades to aircraft already in service.
spending.Torpedoes and Related Equipment: MK-48 heavyweight and MK-54 lightweight torpedoes.
spending.Other Weapons: Guns, gun mounts and related weapons.
spending.Industrial Base Activities: Investments in shipyards and suppliers to raise submarine and surface-ship production rates.
spending.Ships Support Equipment: Ship maintenance, modernization, sensors and hull, mechanical and electrical upgrades.
spending.Aviation Support Equipment: Equipment that supports Navy aircraft operations, such as launch and recovery gear.
spending.Ordnance Support Equipment: Equipment for handling and supporting ship weapons systems.
spending.Tracked Combat Vehicles: Abrams tanks, Bradleys, Paladin howitzers and Armored Multi-Purpose Vehicles.
spending.Weapons and Other Combat Vehicles: Stryker upgrades, small arms and other combat equipment.
spending.Ammunition Production Base Support: Modernizing and maintaining government-owned ammunition plants.
spending.Tactical and Support Vehicles: Trucks, Joint Light Tactical Vehicles and other wheeled vehicles.
spending.Communications and Electronics Equipment: Radios, networks, sensors and command-and-control systems.
spending.Other Support Equipment: Engineering, training, construction and other support equipment.
spending.Virginia Class Submarine: Fast-attack nuclear submarines, built jointly by General Dynamics Electric Boat (Groton, Connecticut and Quonset Point, Rhode Island) and HII Newport News.
spending.COLUMBIA Class Submarine: Ballistic missile submarines that replace the Ohio class, led by General Dynamics Electric Boat. The Navy's top acquisition priority.
spending.DDG-51: Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyers, built at Bath Iron Works in Maine and HII Ingalls in Mississippi.
spending.TAO Fleet Oiler: John Lewis-class fleet oilers that refuel ships at sea.
spending.Medium Landing Ship: A new, smaller amphibious ship to move Marines between islands and coastlines.
spending.CVN Refueling Overhauls: Midlife nuclear refueling and overhaul of Nimitz-class aircraft carriers.
spending.Carrier Replacement Program: Gerald R. Ford-class aircraft carriers built at HII Newport News.
spending.CVN-81: The future USS Doris Miller, a Ford-class aircraft carrier.
spending.Joint Strike Fighter CV: F-35C, the carrier-based version of the F-35.
spending.JSF STOVL: F-35B, the short-takeoff, vertical-landing version flown by the Marine Corps.
spending.CH-53K (Heavy Lift): CH-53K King Stallion heavy-lift helicopters from Sikorsky.
spending.E-2D Adv Hawkeye: E-2D Advanced Hawkeye carrier-based airborne early warning aircraft.
spending.KC-130J: KC-130J tanker and transport aircraft for the Marine Corps.
spending.Trident II Mods: Life extension and production of Trident II D5 submarine-launched ballistic missiles.
spending.Standard Missile: SM-6 and other Standard Missiles for fleet air and missile defense.
spending.LRASM: Long Range Anti-Ship Missile, a stealthy anti-ship cruise missile.
spending.ESSM: Evolved SeaSparrow Missile for ship self-defense.
spending.Tomahawk: Tomahawk land-attack and maritime strike cruise missiles.
spending.Tomahawk Mods: Upgrades to Tomahawk missiles already in inventory.
spending.Next Generation Fighter: F/A-XX, the Navy's planned sixth-generation carrier fighter.
spending.Nuclear-Armed Sea-Launched Cruise Missil: Development of a new nuclear-armed cruise missile for submarines.
spending.TACAMO Modernization: The E-130J aircraft replacing the E-6B Mercury, which relays orders to ballistic missile submarines.
spending.CONVENTIONAL PROMPT STRIKE (CPS): The Navy's hypersonic boost-glide missile for Zumwalt-class destroyers and Virginia-class submarines.
spending.CHALK CORAL: A program known publicly only by its code name; its details are classified.
spending.PILOT FISH: A program known publicly only by its code name; its details are classified.
spending.RETRACT MAPLE: A program known publicly only by its code name; its details are classified.
spending.Submarine Industrial Base: Funding to expand shipyard and supplier capacity for Columbia and Virginia-class submarine production.
spending.Surface Ship Industrial Base: Funding to expand shipyard and supplier capacity for surface ships.
spending.Ship Maintenance, Repair and Modernizati: Equipment and modernization work installed during ship maintenance periods.
spending.Medium Unmanned Surface Vehicle (MUSVs): Uncrewed surface vessels for surveillance and other missions.
spending.Amphibious Combat Vehicle Family of Vehi: Amphibious Combat Vehicles from BAE Systems, replacing the Marines' AAV.
spending.Ground Based Air Defense: Marine Corps short-range air defense against drones, cruise missiles and aircraft.
spending.Naval Strike Missile (NSM): Anti-ship missiles for the Marine Corps' ground-launched NMESIS system.
spending.UH-60 Blackhawk M Model (MYP): UH-60M Black Hawk utility helicopters from Sikorsky, bought under a multiyear contract.
spending.CH-47 Helicopter: CH-47F Chinook heavy-lift helicopters from Boeing.
spending.AH-64 Apache Block IIIA Reman: Remanufacturing older Apaches into the AH-64E configuration.
spending.MSE Missile: PAC-3 MSE interceptors for the Patriot air and missile defense system, from Lockheed Martin.
spending.Guided MLRS Rocket (GMLRS): GPS-guided rockets fired from HIMARS and M270 launchers.
spending.Patriot Mods: Upgrades to Patriot air and missile defense systems.
spending.LONG-RANGE HYPERSONIC WEAPON: Dark Eagle, the Army's ground-launched hypersonic missile.
spending.M-SHORAD - Procurement: Maneuver short-range air defense systems mounted on Stryker vehicles.
spending.Armored Multi Purpose Vehicle (AMPV): Replacement for the M113 armored personnel carrier.
spending.Next Generation Squad Weapon: The XM7 rifle and XM250 automatic rifle replacing the M4 and M249.
spending.Industrial Facilities: Modernizing the Army's government-owned ammunition plants.
spending.Future Long Range Assault Aircraft Devel: The MV-75 tiltrotor from Bell, replacing many Black Hawks.
spending.Hypersonics EMD: Engineering and manufacturing development for the Dark Eagle hypersonic missile.
spending.Army Kwajalein Atoll: The Reagan Test Site in the Marshall Islands, used for missile defense and space tracking tests.
spending.IAMD Battle Command System: IBCS, which links Army air and missile defense radars and launchers into one network.
spending.Aircraft Procurement, Air Force › Combat: Fighters and bombers: F-35A, F-15EX and the B-21 Raider.
spending.Aircraft Procurement, Air Force › Airlif: Tankers and transports: KC-46A and C-130J.
spending.Aircraft Procurement, Air Force › Traine: Pilot training aircraft, mainly the T-7A Red Hawk.
spending.Aircraft Procurement, Air Force › Other: Special-purpose aircraft such as the E-7 Wedgetail, helicopters and drones.
spending.Missile Procurement, Air Force › Other M: Tactical missiles such as AMRAAM, JASSM and the Long Range Anti-Ship Missile.
spending.Missile Procurement, Air Force › Ballist: Minuteman III upkeep and related ballistic missile procurement.
spending.Other Procurement, Air Force › Other Bas: Base equipment plus the large classified procurement line, which accounts for nearly all of this activity.
spending.RDT&E, Air Force › Advanced Component De: Building and testing prototypes of new systems before full development. The B-21 and E-7 are budgeted here.
spending.RDT&E, Air Force › System Development an: Engineering and manufacturing development of systems headed for production. Sentinel and the F-47 are budgeted here.
spending.RDT&E, Air Force › Operational System De: Upgrades to systems already fielded, plus most classified R&D. For the Air Force this includes F-35, B-52 and F-22 upgrades.
spending.Procurement, Space Force › Space Procure: Satellites and launch services: National Security Space Launch, GPS, missile-warning and communications satellites.
spending.Auxiliaries Craft and Prior Year Program: Support ships such as oilers and salvage ships, small craft, and cost growth on ships funded in earlier years.
spending.Not itemized in public account data: Spending Treasury reports for this title that USAspending does not break out by account. Most of it is classified activity, such as intelligence agencies funded through Defense-wide accounts.
spending.Operating Forces: Running combat units: flying hours, ship operations, unit training, depot maintenance and base support.
spending.Mobilization: Prepositioned equipment, sealift and airlift readiness, and activating reserve forces.
spending.Training and Recruiting: Basic and specialized training, flight training, service academies, ROTC and recruiting.
spending.Administration and Service Wide Activiti: Headquarters, logistics, security programs, IT and other service-wide functions.
spending.Administration and Servicewide Activitie: Headquarters, logistics, security programs, IT and other service-wide functions.
spending.Pay and Allowances of Officers: Basic pay, housing and subsistence allowances, special pays and retirement accrual for officers.
spending.Pay and Allowances of Enlisted Personnel: Basic pay, housing and subsistence allowances, bonuses and retirement accrual for enlisted members.
spending.Pay and Allowances of Enlisted: Basic pay, housing and subsistence allowances, bonuses and retirement accrual for enlisted members.
spending.Pay and Allowances of Cadets: Pay for cadets and midshipmen at the service academies.
spending.Subsistence of Enlisted Personnel: Food for enlisted members, through dining facilities and subsistence allowances.
spending.Permanent Change of Station Travel: Moving service members and their families to new duty stations.
spending.Other Military Personnel Costs: Unemployment benefits, death gratuities, education benefits and other personnel costs.
spending.Basic Pay: The base salary set by rank and years of service.
spending.Basic Allowance for Housing: Tax-free housing allowance that varies by location, rank and family status.
spending.Retired Pay Accrual: The service's payment into the Military Retirement Fund for future pensions, counted as a personnel cost today.
spending.Major Construction: Projects above $9 million, the threshold for minor construction, each approved individually by Congress. Grouped here by state or country.
spending.Minor Construction: Smaller projects below the threshold for individual approval.
spending.Design: Planning and design work for future construction projects.
spending.Construction Improvements: Renovating and improving existing family housing.
spending.Defense Health Program: The military health system: military hospitals and clinics, and TRICARE payments to civilian providers for service members, families and retirees.
spending.Golden Dome for America Fund: Funding from the 2025 reconciliation law for Golden Dome, a planned layered missile defense system for the U.S. homeland.
spending.Operation and Maintenance, Defense-Wide: Defense agencies and offices: special operations, the Defense Logistics Agency, DoD schools, intelligence agencies and more.
spending.RDT&E, Defense-Wide: R&D by defense agencies: the Missile Defense Agency, DARPA, special operations, Office of the Secretary of Defense programs and classified work.
spending.Ship Operations: Fuel, maintenance and operating costs for Navy ships at sea and in port.
spending.Air Operations: Flying hours, aircraft maintenance and depot repair for Navy and Marine Corps aircraft.
spending.Base Support: Running bases: utilities, facilities, security and services.
spending.Land Forces: Training and operating Army combat units.
spending.Land Forces Readiness: Equipment maintenance and readiness for Army units.
spending.Land Forces Readiness Support: Base operations and facilities that support Army units.
spending.Air Operations › Flying Hour Program: Fuel, parts and maintenance for flying hours.
spending.Combat Related Operations: Air Force combat units, global C3I and early warning.
spending.Space Operations: Operating satellites, launch ranges and space control systems.

revenue.Individual Income Taxes: Federal income tax paid by individuals on wages, investment income and business income passed through to owners.
revenue.Withheld from paychecks: Income tax taken out of paychecks by employers throughout the year.
revenue.Estimated & final payments (not withheld: Quarterly estimated payments and payments made with tax returns, mainly from self-employment and investment income.
revenue.Presidential Election Campaign Fund: Taxpayers' optional $3 designations to public financing of presidential campaigns.
revenue.Social Insurance and Retirement Receipts: Payroll taxes that fund Social Security, Medicare Part A and unemployment insurance, plus federal employees' retirement contributions.
revenue.Employment and General Retirement: Social Security and Medicare payroll taxes and railroad retirement taxes.
revenue.Federal Old-Age and Survivors Insurance: The retirement and survivors portion of the 12.4% Social Security payroll tax, split between employers and workers.
revenue.Federal Disability Insurance Trust Fund: The disability portion of the Social Security payroll tax.
revenue.Federal Hospital Insurance Trust Fund: The 2.9% Medicare payroll tax, plus an extra 0.9% on high earners.
revenue.Federal Insurance Contributions Act Taxe: FICA: payroll taxes withheld from employees' wages and matched by employers.
revenue.Self-Employment Contributions Act Taxes: SECA: the self-employed pay both the worker and employer shares of payroll tax.
revenue.Receipts from Railroad Retirement Board: Medicare payroll taxes collected on railroad workers.
revenue.Railroad Retirement: Payroll taxes paid by railroad workers and employers in place of Social Security taxes.
revenue.Rail Pension and Supplemental Annuity: Railroad payroll taxes for the private-pension-like tier of railroad retirement.
revenue.Social Security Equivalent Account: Railroad payroll taxes equivalent to Social Security taxes.
revenue.Deposits by States: State unemployment taxes that employers pay to states, which states deposit in the federal Unemployment Trust Fund.
revenue.Federal Unemployment Taxes: FUTA: the federal unemployment tax on employers, which pays for program administration and loans to states.
revenue.Railroad Unemployment Taxes: Unemployment taxes for the railroad industry.
revenue.Federal Employees' Retirement--Employee: Pension contributions taken from federal employees' pay.
revenue.Non-Federal Employees Retirement: Retirement contributions from a few non-federal groups covered by federal plans.
revenue.Corporation Income Taxes: Federal tax on corporate profits, currently at a 21% rate.
revenue.Customs Duties: Tariffs on imported goods. In FY2026, large refunds followed the Supreme Court ruling that struck down many tariffs imposed in 2025.
revenue.Excise Taxes: Taxes on specific goods and activities, such as fuel, alcohol, tobacco and airline tickets.
revenue.Highway Trust Fund: Federal fuel taxes (18.4 cents per gallon on gasoline, 24.4 on diesel) and truck taxes, which pay for highways and transit.
revenue.Miscellaneous Excise Taxes: Taxes on alcohol, tobacco, health insurance plans, firearms and other items.
revenue.Airport and Airway Trust Fund: Taxes on airline tickets, cargo and aviation fuel, which pay for the FAA.
revenue.Black Lung Disability Trust Fund: A tax on coal that pays benefits to miners disabled by black lung disease.
revenue.Estate and Gift Taxes: Tax on large estates and gifts above a high exemption.
revenue.Miscellaneous Receipts: Fees, fines, Federal Reserve earnings and other collections.
revenue.Deposit of Earnings, Federal Reserve Sys: Profits the Federal Reserve sends to the Treasury after covering its costs. Since 2022 the Fed has mostly run operating losses, because the interest it pays on bank reserves exceeds what it earns, so these payments have been small.
revenue.Universal Service Fund: Fees phone companies pay into the FCC's Universal Service Fund.
revenue.All Other: Fines, penalties, fees and other miscellaneous collections.
revenue.Adjustments Attributable to Prior Years-: Corrections to earlier years' self-employment tax estimates.
Corrections to earlier years' payroll tax estimates.

functions.Medicare: Health insurance for people 65 and older and some people with disabilities.
functions.Net Interest: Interest on the debt, minus interest the government earns. This now exceeds defense spending.
functions.Health: Medicaid, CHIP, ACA subsidies, NIH, CDC and other health programs other than Medicare.
functions.National Defense: The military, plus nuclear weapons programs at the Department of Energy.
functions.Income Security: Federal retirement, unemployment, food assistance, SSI, housing aid and refundable tax credits.
functions.Veterans Benefits and Services: Veterans' disability compensation, health care, education and housing benefits.
functions.Administration of Justice: Federal law enforcement, courts and prisons.
functions.Education, Training, Employment, and Soc: K-12 grants, college student aid, job training and social services.
functions.Community and Regional Development: Disaster relief, community development grants and rural development.
functions.Natural Resources and Environment: Public lands, parks, water projects, conservation and pollution control.
functions.Agriculture: Farm income support and crop insurance.
functions.General Science, Space, and Technology: NASA, the National Science Foundation and DOE science.
functions.General Government: Congress, the White House, tax collection and central government operations.
functions.Energy: Energy research, power marketing and energy loan programs.
functions.Commerce and Housing Credit: Mortgage insurance, the Postal Service and business lending. Often negative because fees and premiums exceed costs.
functions.Undistributed Offsetting Receipts: Receipts not assigned to any function, such as offshore oil and gas royalties and agencies' payments to employee retirement funds.

states.Federal taxes paid: Federal taxes attributed to the state's residents and businesses using the Comptroller's allocation method (customs duties and miscellaneous receipts are not allocated).
states.Federal spending received: Federal spending that flows to the state's residents, governments and businesses.
states.Individual income tax: Federal income tax paid by the state's residents, after refunds.
states.Payroll taxes (Social Security, Medicare: Social Security, Medicare and unemployment taxes on wages earned in the state.
states.Corporate income tax: Corporate income tax attributed to the state under the Comptroller's allocation method, which draws on IRS corporate return data.
states.Excise taxes: Federal taxes on fuel, alcohol, tobacco and other goods, based on in-state consumption.
states.Estate and gift tax: Federal estate and gift tax paid by the state's residents.
states.Direct payments to people: Benefits paid directly to individuals: Social Security, Medicare, veterans' and retiree benefits, SNAP and refundable tax credits.
states.Social Security: Retirement, survivors and disability benefits paid to residents.
states.Medicare: Medicare payments for residents' health care.
states.Veterans' benefits: Disability compensation, pensions and education benefits for veterans living in the state.
states.Federal retiree benefits: Pensions and health benefits for retired federal civilian employees and military retirees.
states.Student loan costs: The federal cost of student loans to residents.
states.Supplemental Security Income: Cash assistance to low-income aged, blind or disabled residents.
states.Earned Income Tax Credit (refundable): Refunds to low- and moderate-income working families beyond the tax they owed.
states.Child Tax Credit (refundable): Refunds to families with children beyond the tax they owed.
states.Other direct payments: Remaining direct payments to individuals not listed separately.
states.Grants to state and local governments: Federal grants to state governments, localities, schools and transit agencies. Medicaid is by far the largest.
states.Medicaid: The federal share of the state's Medicaid program.
states.Housing assistance: Section 8 rental assistance and public housing funding.
states.Child nutrition (school meals): School lunch, breakfast and summer meal programs.
states.Children's Health Insurance Program (CHI: Health coverage for children in families that earn too much for Medicaid.
states.K-12 education (Title I): Grants to schools serving many low-income students.
states.TANF (cash assistance): Block grants for cash assistance and work programs for low-income families.
states.Special education: Grants for educating students with disabilities.
states.Education Stabilization Fund (pandemic a: Remaining pandemic-era relief funds for schools and colleges, now winding down.
states.Highway infrastructure programs: Additional highway funding, largely from the 2021 infrastructure law.
states.Other grants: All other federal grants to the state, local governments and nonprofits.
states.Federal contracts: Payments to businesses in the state for goods and services the government buys. Counted where the work is performed by the prime contractor.
states.Defense contracts: Defense Department contracts for weapons, equipment, services and construction performed in the state.
states.Federal employee wages: Pay for federal civilian employees and military personnel stationed in the state.
states.Small-business disaster loans (EIDL): Federal costs from Economic Injury Disaster Loans to businesses, a program greatly expanded during the pandemic.
